Join me as I dive into the chaotic jungle of open data, GIS wizardry, and the satisfying tutorials that kept me (barely) sane during my researcher struggles!

![](https://media.giphy.com/media/citBl9yPwnUOs/giphy.gif){width=50% fig-align="center"}

## Open spatial data

- [Natural earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/): Free vector and raster maps of cultural and physical data for the whole world. 
I use the natural earth data mainly to get administrative boundaries of countries, states or provinces. They also have coarse resolution rivers and lakes.

- [Open topography](https://www.opentopography.org/): Global and regional elevetion models, and so much more!
Amazing DEM at a global and regional scale. They also have bulk download available if you register for free! 😎

- [Landsat ready data](https://glad.geog.umd.edu/ard/home) Spatially and temporally consistent input for land cover mapping and change detection at global to local scales

## Tools

### Landscape ecology

- I used [Gnarly Landscape Utilities](https://circuitscape.org/gnarly-landscape-utilities/) to create resistance surfaces for my master's thesis. In the webpage you can download the tool and also tutorials provided by circuitscape.

- The one and only [Linkage mapper](https://linkagemapper.org/) for delimiting corridors.

- [Circuitscape](https://circuitscape.org/) and [omniscape](https://docs.circuitscape.org/Omniscape.jl/latest/) for modeling functional connectivity based on circuit theory

- [Conefor](conefor.org) and [Makurhini](https://connectscape.github.io/Makurhini/) to model landscape conenctivity based on graph theory

- [Landscape metrics](https://r-spatialecology.github.io/landscapemetrics/) Incredibly useful R package to calculate landscape metrics


## Open datasets

- [Avonet](https://opentraits.org/datasets/avonet.html): Functional trait data for all birds, including six ecological variables, eleven continuous morphological traits, and information on range size and location.
